title: Holy, Holy, Holy
summary: When the days grind on and you ask, "What is this for?", the remedy isn't a new method. It is a vision of God, and in that vision we see Christ.
exhortation: Does your soul ever feel a strange, hollow ache, as if you walked into a theater in the middle of the second act and can't figure out the plot? The days grind on, one into the next like the heavy gears of a millstone. Your feet hit the floor in the morning, and the question hits you before the coffee does: what is this for? What am I doing?

If you feel you're missing something, it's probably because you are. You may have lost the thread and forgotten the grand design. Perhaps you're like Isaiah: counted among God's people, a defender of the faith. You speak holy things, advocate his laws and champion his ways. Yet in the quiet of your own heart you whisper, "What am I doing?"

The remedy is not a new method or a better schedule. The remedy is a vision. You need to see what Isaiah saw. His eyes were opened to a God who is utterly transcendent, high and lifted up, seated on a throne beyond the reach of human imagination. He saw a glory so blinding that his only natural response was the honest cry of a dying man: "Woe is me!" He expected to be consumed, to vanish like mist before the furnace of God's holiness. He thought that to see the unseeable with sinful eyes was a death sentence, and he wasn't wrong.

But our God does not delight in destroying the broken. He doesn't send fire to consume us. He sends a coal to purify. And where Isaiah saw an angel, we see the Son. We see Christ. He is the missing piece. When the grind of life wears the soul thin, Jesus is what fills the void. He isn't merely a character in the story. He is the point of the story. He is the mediator who laid a hand on God and man and intercedes for us even now. So stop wandering through the fog of your own routine. Lift your eyes this morning and see the God who is both terrifyingly majestic and tenderly compassionate toward us. If your days feel like a blur, look long at the throne of God. Let's find our purpose again and behold the Messiah who has come, the Savior who bridged the gap, the King who calls us his own.
prayer: Lord, if not for your cleansing blood, without that coal touching our lips, we would be utterly lost. It is an amazing thing that sinful human beings are allowed to sing your praises and enter your presence. All of this is just a foretaste of when we are raised with you in glory and sin is gone for good. What a time of worship that will be.

And we can be confident that this is our future, because you came, died, conquered death and shed your blood for our forgiveness, so that we might be clean, pure and holy before you. Fill us with hope and strength for the day ahead, so that we honor and glorify you with our lives today, walking not in our own power but in yours. In Jesus' name.
